subject: Grid pricing, geo anchoring and reseller passback — CloudHub PO
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@cloudhub.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudhub.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Grid pricing, geo anchoring and reseller passback for CloudHub PO

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is keen to move to a private offer. Procurement has a few open questions before we can formalize the PO schedule:

1) We need clarification on how your list price "grid" will be anchored across regions. Our legal requires explicit floors for EU public sector purchases. Are list prices the same across us/eu/apac or do you apply region multipliers?

2) How do reseller passback/commission amounts flow? We work with local resellers in the EU and need to understand whether commissions are taken as a percent of list price or net revenue after discounts.

3) VAT and invoicing: will Redwood invoice CloudHub (net of VAT) and our reseller invoice downstream, or do you have a pass-through arrangement?

We can share an internal PO schedule (attached) and would like a short written confirmation on the above points to include in our procurement packet.

Attached: CloudHub_PO_Schedule.pdf

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Procurement — CloudHub Systems

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Grid pricing, geo anchoring and reseller passback for CloudHub PO

Hi Maria — looping in Ben (sales lead) and Naomi (revops/finance) to get firm answers. Quick notes for context: CloudHub is asking for a private offer covering multi-region list-pricing floors (esp EU public sector) and a clear passback mechanism for their resellers.

Ben/Naomi — can you confirm:
- Whether we default to a single global list price or maintain regional list floors (and what multipliers we use for EU/APAC).
- Commission routing: do we treat reseller commissions as a reduction to list price (i.e., reported as discount) or a separately tracked channel credit? Finance will need to know taxable flows for VAT.

I can host a 30-min call with Maria next week if that helps.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Channel Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@cloudhub.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Grid pricing, geo anchoring and reseller passback for CloudHub PO

Irene / Naomi / Maria — drafting a concise response and attaching a proposed pricing waterfall (see proposal_grid_pricing_v2.xlsx). High-level summary below:

- Regional list price approach: we publish a base global list price and apply region anchors for public-sector sensitivity. For EU public sector we typically set an EU list floor that is 8-12% below the global list to reflect local procurement norms, not to be used as a sales discount without approval.

- Reseller commissions / passback: we prefer to model commissions as a separate partner rebate (tracked in our finance system) rather than burying them within a negotiated list discount. In practice we:
  * Issue invoice to primary buyer (CloudHub) at net after any negotiated private-offer discount.
  * Record reseller commission as a contra-revenue / rebate paid to the reseller and tracked for reporting. This keeps list price visible and keeps tax treatment clearer for VAT.

- VAT handling: Redwood invoices CloudHub net of VAT where applicable; reseller payments/rebates are handled between Redwood and the reseller (we provide documentation to CloudHub showing the rebate mechanics). If CloudHub requires pass-through invoicing, that is an exception we can evaluate but needs legal + tax sign-off.

Open asks for CloudHub (Maria):
- Confirm whether the EU floor needs to be codified in the PO language (we can add a clause).
- Provide a list of resellers and whether they invoice CloudHub directly or invoice via CloudHub's partner aggregator.

Next steps:
- Naomi, can you validate the proposed rebate-as-contra-revenue flow with finance and confirm VAT treatment?
- If acceptable, I propose we send an updated private-offer term sheet with two lines: negotiated net price and an annex that defines the EU list floor and reseller rebate mechanics.

Attaching: proposal_grid_pricing_v2.xlsx (contains suggested grid, waterfall, sample clause).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@cloudhub.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudhub.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Grid pricing, geo anchoring and reseller passback for CloudHub PO

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement after reviewing the spreadsheet:

- The EU floor needs to be explicit in the PO; our legal won't sign without it for public-sector orders. Can you add a short clause in the annex stating: "Vendor agrees to maintain a published EU list floor for public sector purchases of Product X for the duration of the PO."

- Reseller routing: our resellers will often invoice CloudHub directly and expect Redwood to pay them commissions. The rebate-as-contra-revenue model is acceptable, but we need an example invoice flow in writing showing how Redwood will record the rebate and evidence we will receive to include in our vendor file.

- VAT: we'll need a short note confirming Redwood will provide documentation (rebate ledgers / rebate receipts) sufficient for CloudHub to justify downstream VAT accounting.

Attached our internal procurement schedule for projected milestones.

Would appreciate a short written annex and a sample invoice flow diagram (one page) we can attach to the PO packet. Happy to take a 30-minute walkthrough early next week.
